title: the release core's steps and rows are named by their position (step 6, row 9, steps 7 to 11) in its messages, docs, pages and tests, against hv's rule that nothing is named by its position in a list
body:
Found by vc on 2026-10-23 with the docs' count scan (the issue filed beside this one). hv's rule in the user-scope AGENTS.md: "nothing is named by its position in a list (`check 14`): such numbers mean nothing, and are wrong as soon as something is added."

The release core numbers its steps, and devbin names them by number almost everywhere: "step 6 asks", "row 9 reads", "steps 7 to 11", "rows 6, 7 and 11", "steps 10 and 11 report rather than stop", "It runs every step, 1 to 11". Measured on main at 51b361dd with `LC_ALL=C grep -o -i -E '(step|steps|row|rows) [0-9]+'`: docs/ 45, lib/pages 7, lib/cmd/release, lib/release.steps and lib/release.notes 172 (printed messages and comments), tests/unit 173 (titles, assertions and comments). A step added anywhere but the end renumbers every later one, and each of those sites goes wrong at once.

Every step already has a name, which the docs list: resolve, pre-flight, stamp, commit, gates, confirm, tag, push, object, after, ci.

Smaller cases of the same kind: docs/authoring-commands.md:37 "Orders 2 and 3 sit above order 4" and :65 "steps 2 and 3 never both answer" (the resolution order's list); docs/migration.md:118 "Steps 1 through 4 are reversible"; lib/pages/iex.md:18 and lib/pages/server.md:28 "either of the first two".

**Fix:** name each step by its name in printed messages, docs, pages and test titles ("the confirm step", "the object row"), and print the step table by name. Whether the table keeps a number column at all is for the builder to propose and review to rule, since a printed number invites "row 9" again. Tests that read the table read rows by name. The smaller cases name what they mean.

Not a behaviour change: the steps, their order and their postconditions stay as they are. It is a large edit across the release core, its docs and its tests, so it is filed on its own to be batched as hv's directive 13 says.


## Resolution

Fixed at 193c2107, on landing suite 20261024-1756 at 62c632b4 (2474 of 2474 ok, 5 environmental skips, the errors seal empty), with the fleet-less candidate suite 20261024-1805 from the same tip (2319 of 2319 ok, 5 environmental skips, the errors seal empty). cc built it in a scratch clone, and vc landed it.

- `_RELEASE_STEP_NAMES` (lib/release.steps) is the one place the core's order is written. release_row, cut_row, cut_fail and cut_call take a step's name (`cut_row object ...`), and a name that is no step's dies as a devbin defect naming the steps. That arm was red on the base.
- OUTPUT CHANGE, declared: the status table and a cut's summary print no number column. A row is `  <step>  <state>  <detail>`, its name and state columns as wide as the longest step name and state. The stop line reads "stopped at the <step> step". No known reader reads the table by column: Intent declares release.verbs [check, attach].
- The core's messages and comments, docs/releasing.md, docs/configuration.md and the release page name each step. The smaller cases name what they mean: authoring-commands.md's resolution orders and the help sources' references in lib/resolve, lib/help and config.reference.yaml; migration.md's headings and its references to the delete; the iex and server pages.
- The suite's readers (row_of, state_of, assert_state, assert_stopped_at) take a step's name. row_of matches a row's own shape and takes the last one, so neither a step's own output nor attach's own table is read as a core row. The status order arm reads its names from `_RELEASE_STEP_NAMES`.
- Not renamed: the "issue 0088, row 2" and "row 3" citations, which name rows of that issue's table.
